s: A solutions architect has launched multiple Amazon EC2 instances in a placement group within a single Availability Zone. Because of additional load on the system, the solutions architect attempts to add new instances to the placement group. However, the solutions architect receives an insufficient capacity error. What should the solutions architect do to troubleshoot this issue?
o: Use a spread placement group. Set a minimum of eight instances for each Availability Zone.
Stop and start all the instances in the placement group. Try the launch again.
Create a new placement group. Merge the new placement group with the original placement group.
Launch the additional instances as Dedicated Hosts in the placement groups.

w.y: A cluster placement group in one AZ packs instances onto closely placed hardware, so adding instances later can hit insufficient capacity. AWS recommends stopping and starting all instances in the group, which may move them to hardware with room for every instance, and then retrying the launch.

o.A: Spread placement groups allow at most seven running instances per AZ, so 'eight per AZ' is impossible, and spreading also gives up low latency.
o.B: Correct: stop and start all instances so EC2 can re-place the whole group on hardware with enough capacity, then retry.
o.D: Dedicated Hosts do not solve cluster placement capacity, and cluster placement groups do not support Dedicated Hosts.
